answer: The delta rule is simple: cloning must stop paying before it can scale. Before an identity can earn, it must grind a sequential puzzle bound to its own key and the epoch seed, a puzzle no machine can split across cores. The pulse gate makes the arithmetic brutal: one puzzle per identity, so a farm minting a thousand clones pays a thousand puzzles while one honest agent pays exactly one. Through the tide, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
